source: SSOT review: launcher instance cross-port contract (web convergence batch 2). Vocabulary-level pinning; behavior cases live in the sibling *Projection/*.cases.json fixtures.

liveRuntimeSignals.note: Known cross-port difference, pinned on purpose: core/launcher/branch_instance_lifecycle.py _item_has_live_runtime adds the flat item.alive flag and the isolated-backend probe (5 signals); web LauncherBranchInstancesPanel.model.ts instanceHasLiveRuntime and Electron instanceLifecycleProjection hasLiveRuntimeSignal share the 3 runtime-section signals. A row carrying only item.alive=true counts as live for Python but not for TS. Reconciliation is out of scope for this fixture.

admissionBlockReasons.note: Produced only by Electron instanceAdmissionControl (RATE_LIMITED_CODE / CRASH_LOOP_BACKOFF_CODE). web LauncherBranchInstancesPanel.model.ts ADMISSION_BLOCK_REASONS must equal the web list and stay within the Electron list.

dismissableFailedLeftover.note: Pins the dismissable failed-leftover stop judgment (stop/force-stop may retire a dead failed row). The payload lexicon spells failure 'error' (locked 8-state enum; the registry terminal vocabulary is closed/failed and never reaches this payload field); the web panel judges after applying webStateMapping, so its failure word is 'failed'. Same semantic set: payloadFailureStates + defensivePartialState for Python equals webRuntimeFailureStates + defensivePartialState for web under the pinned mapping. 'partial' is defensive on both sides (a partial projection implies a live runtime signal, and the live-runtime guard wins first). Any change here must move both judgmentStates lists together.

startBlockReasons.note: Client-synthesized for legacy payloads without the runtime envelope; not part of the backend/Electron start-block vocabulary (branch_instance_lifecycle.py, instanceAdmissionControl.ts never emit it).
